Question 1. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: The principal, (A) / along with all the teachers, (B) / were attending the meeting (C) / in the main conference hall. (D)

 Sentence II: Not only the students (A) / but also the class teacher (B) / were pleased with (C) / the final sports results.(D) 'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — were attending; Sentence II: Part C — were pleased with
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: was attending; Sentence II: was pleased with
explanation: Rule 1: Phrases such as 'along with', 'as well as', and 'together with' do not change the number of the main subject.
Rule 2: With 'not only...but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it.

Application: Sentence I has the singular subject 'principal', so 'were attending' should be 'was attending'. In Sentence II, the nearer subject is the singular 'class teacher', so 'were pleased' should be 'was pleased'.
Correct sentence I: The principal, along with all the teachers, was attending the meeting in the main conference hall.
Correct sentence II: Not only the students but also the class teacher was pleased with the final sports results.

Question 2. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Each of the (A) / submitted assignments (B) / have been evaluated (C) / by the subject expert. (D)

Sentence II: Neither of the (A) / two applicant candidates (B) / were qualified for (C) / the final interview round.(D) 'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — have been evaluated; Sentence II: Part C — were qualified for
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: has been evaluated; Sentence II: was qualified for
explanation: Rule 1: 'Each of' followed by a plural noun takes a singular verb.
Rule 2: In formal subject-verb agreement questions, 'neither of' followed by a plural noun generally takes a singular verb.
Application: 'Each' and 'neither' are singular in these constructions, so 'have' changes to 'has' and 'were' changes to 'was'.
Correct sentence I: Each of the submitted assignments has been evaluated by the subject expert.
Correct sentence II: Neither of the two applicant candidates was qualified for the final interview round.

Question 3. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Either of the master chefs (A) / cook the main course (B) / when the restaurant (C) / gets busy on weekends. (D)

Sentence II: The head chef prepares (A) / the starter items, (B) / but the assistant cooks (C) / prepares the desserts. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part B — cook the main course; Sentence II: Part D — prepares the desserts
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: cooks the main course; Sentence II: prepare the desserts
explanation: Rule 1: 'Either of' followed by a plural noun takes a singular verb in standard exam grammar.
Rule 2: A plural subject takes a plural verb.
Application: Sentence I requires 'cooks' because the subject is 'Either'. In Sentence II, 'assistant cooks' is plural, so 'prepares' should be 'prepare'.
Correct sentence I: Either of the master chefs cooks the main course when the restaurant gets busy on weekends.
Correct sentence II: The head chef prepares the starter items, but the assistant cooks prepare the desserts.

Question 4. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Everybody in (A) / the auditorium (B) / were standing up (C) / to applaud the performers. (D)

Sentence II: A lot of valuable time (A) / were wasted while (B) / waiting for the (C) / chief guest to arrive. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — were standing up; Sentence II: Part B — were wasted while
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: was standing up; Sentence II: was wasted while
explanation: Rule 1: Indefinite pronouns such as 'everybody', 'everyone', and 'someone' take singular verbs.
Rule 2: 'Time' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb in this context.
Application: 'Everybody' requires 'was standing'. The expression 'a lot of valuable time' also requires 'was wasted'.
Correct sentence I: Everybody in the auditorium was standing up to applaud the performers.
Correct sentence II: A lot of valuable time was wasted while waiting for the chief guest to arrive.

Question 5. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: There is a few milk (A) / left in the jug, (B) / so you can make (C) / a cup of tea. (D)

Sentence II: The government believes (A) / that the rich is (B) / responsible for helping (C) / the underprivileged communities. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part A — a few milk; Sentence II: Part B — the rich is
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: a little milk; Sentence II: the rich are
explanation: Rule 1: Use 'a little' with uncountable nouns and 'a few' with plural countable nouns.
Rule 2: 'The + adjective', when referring to a group of people, takes a plural verb.
Application: 'Milk' is uncountable, so 'a few milk' should be 'a little milk'. 'The rich' refers to rich people as a group, so 'is' should be 'are'.
Correct sentence I: There is a little milk left in the jug, so you can make a cup of tea.
Correct sentence II: The government believes that the rich are responsible for helping the underprivileged communities.

Question 6. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Rohan is one of (A) / those bright students (B) / who always scores (C) / top marks in physics. (D)

Sentence II: Neither the captain (A) / nor his teammates (B) / was present at (C) / the press conference. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — who always scores; Sentence II: Part C — was present at
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: who always score; Sentence II: were present at
explanation: Rule 1: In the construction 'one of those + plural noun + who', the relative pronoun 'who' refers to the plural noun, so it takes a plural verb.
Rule 2: With 'neither...nor', the verb generally agrees with the nearer subject.
Application: 'Who' refers to 'students', so 'scores' should be 'score'. In Sentence II, the nearer subject is 'teammates', which is plural, so 'was' should be 'were'.
Correct sentence I: Rohan is one of those bright students who always score top marks in physics.
Correct sentence II: Neither the captain nor his teammates were present at the press conference.

Question 7. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Each of the (A) / four boys have (B) / brought their own (C) / project materials. (D)

Sentence II: Not only the manager (A) / but also his staff (B) / was working late (C) / to finish the work. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part B — have; Sentence II: Part C — was working late
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: has; Sentence II: were working late
explanation: Rule 1: 'Each of' followed by a plural noun takes a singular verb.
Rule 2: With 'not only...but also', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. In this sentence, 'staff' is intended as a plural group of employees.
Application: 'Each' requires 'has brought'. Since 'his staff' refers to the employees acting individually, 'was working' changes to 'were working'.
Correct sentence I: Each of the four boys has brought their own project materials.
Correct sentence II: Not only the manager but also his staff were working late to finish the work.

Question 8. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: There are a little (A) / students present (B) / in the computer lab (C) / for the practical exam. (D)

Sentence II: The unemployed (A) / is struggling to (B) / find stable jobs (C) / in the current market. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part A — a little; Sentence II: Part B — is struggling to
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: a few; Sentence II: are struggling to
explanation: Rule 1: Use 'a few' with plural countable nouns and 'a little' with uncountable nouns.
Rule 2: 'The unemployed' refers to unemployed people as a group and takes a plural verb.
Application: 'Students' is countable, so 'a little students' should be 'a few students'. 'The unemployed' requires 'are struggling'.
Correct sentence I: There are a few students present in the computer lab for the practical exam.
Correct sentence II: The unemployed are struggling to find stable jobs in the current market.

Question 9. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: The head doctor, (A) / along with two nurses, (B) / were examining (C) / the emergency patient. (D)

Sentence II: Neither of the (A) / two routes lead (B) / directly to the (C) / railway station. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — were examining; Sentence II: Part B — lead
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: was examining; Sentence II: leads
explanation: Rule 1: Phrases such as 'along with' do not change the number of the main subject.
Rule 2: In standard competitive-exam grammar, 'neither of' followed by a plural noun takes a singular verb.
Application: The main subject in Sentence I is 'head doctor', so 'were examining' should be 'was examining'. In Sentence II, 'neither' requires 'leads'.
Correct sentence I: The head doctor, along with two nurses, was examining the emergency patient.
Correct sentence II: Neither of the two routes leads directly to the railway station.

Question 10. Identify the incorrect parts in Sentence I and Sentence II.

Sentence I: Everybody who (A) / attended the workshop (B) / were given a free (C) / participation certificate. (D)

Sentence II: A lot of research work (A) / were required to (B) / complete this (C) / science project. (D)

'Select the correct option pair representing the errors in (Sentence I, Sentence II).'

solution.incorrectPart: Sentence I: Part C — were given a free; Sentence II: Part B — were required to
solution.correctPart: Sentence I: was given a free; Sentence II: was required to
explanation: Rule 1: 'Everybody' is singular and takes a singular verb.
Rule 2: 'Research work' is an uncountable singular expression and takes a singular verb.
Application: 'Were given' should be 'was given', and 'were required' should be 'was required'.
Correct sentence I: Everybody who attended the workshop was given a free participation certificate.
Correct sentence II: A lot of research work was required to complete this science project.
